title: MERGE-RNA: a physics-based model to predict RNA secondary structure ensembles with chemical probing.
data_url: https://github.com/giusSacco/MERGE-RNA (archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20059549); raw reads at ENA PRJEB113043

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the whole 16.8 MB code+data repository and parsed every chemical-probing file in it with my own reader of the RNAFramework .rc binary format. Counted exactly 8 distinct RNA molecules: 5 'structured RNAs' (HCV IRES 370 nucleotides, Vibrio cholerae glycine riboswitch 256, bacterial RNase P type A 363, hc16 ligase 363, Tetrahymena ribozyme 413) each measured at 6 DMS (dimethyl sulfate, a chemical that marks unpaired nucleotides) concentrations x 2 replicates, plus cspA 5' untranslated region (170 nucleotides, 6 runs), the Vibrio vulnificus adenine riboswitch (176 nucleotides, 9 runs, in a 1,050-row comma-separated file with a mut_rate column) and one newly measured designed construct (148 nucleotides, 12 runs). Total distinct nucleotides = 2,259; nucleotide x condition rows = 25,560. Confirmed reference secondary structures exist as dot-bracket strings for only 4 of the 5 structured RNAs (none for RNase P), and read mean sequencing coverage per run (1,365-828,683 reads). Also listed the ENA deposit: 12 nanopore amplicon runs of the single designed construct, 2-66 MB each.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the reference structures for hc16, Tetrahymena ribozyme and the glycine riboswitch came from cryo-EM-guided modelling and were annotated with Barnaba, that the HCV IRES reference was manually transcribed from a figure in another paper, and the reported accuracy comparisons against pseudo-free-energy methods.

a1_downloadable.note: Verified: the GitHub/Zenodo repository is public, MIT-licensed, 16.8 MB, and downloads without login; it contains the processed per-nucleotide mutation-rate files, not just code.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Partly: per-nucleotide DMS mutation rate is a literal column (mut_rate) in the adenine-riboswitch file and is two divisions away in the binary .rc files (mutation counts / coverage, both of which I read). The paper's real output - ensemble populations - is not a measured column anywhere.

a3_inputs_present.note: Verified: full RNA sequences are embedded in every .rc file and in reference.fa, so no accession lookups are needed.

a4_units_stated.note: Verified: mutation rate is a dimensionless fraction of reads, coverage is in reads, DMS concentration is in millimolar in the directory names (0-100 mM), adenine ligand in micromolar, temperature in degrees Celsius.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The unit of learning is the RNA molecule and I counted exactly 8 of them in the files (2,259 distinct nucleotides, reference structures for only 4). The 25,560 nucleotide x condition rows are the same 8 molecules remeasured at 6 probe concentrations x 2 replicates, so effective sample size is 8, far under the ~1,500-row bar; held-out evaluation would have at most 5-8 groups.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Verified: the entire dataset is 24 MB of text, binary count files and four PDB structures.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Verified: the paper says five systems of ~100-400 nucleotides probed at multiple DMS concentrations with replicates; the files show exactly 5 systems, 256-413 nucleotides, 6 concentrations x 2 replicates.

a8_label_provenance.note: Reactivity labels are real sequencing measurements. But the structural reference labels are not measurements: three came from cryo-EM-guided computational modelling, one was hand-transcribed from a published figure, and the ensemble populations the paper reports are MERGE-RNA's own output - using those as labels would be distilling a model.

existing_models.name: MERGE-RNA (this paper's own physics-based model)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reports better base-pair accuracy than pseudo-free-energy methods on the five structured RNAs and recovers NMR-resolved adenine-riboswitch conformations; parameters are fitted jointly on those same few systems, with a leave-one-system-out style demo in the code (3 sequences, 1 held out).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transferability of the fitted physical parameters to sequences outside the training systems, and the lack of reference structures for ensembles (single reference structures are used to score inherently multi-state RNAs).

existing_models.name: RibonanzaNet / RibonanzaNet2 (deep neural networks predicting DMS and 2A3 chemical reactivity from sequence, Das lab)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on 1.1 million crowdsourced sequences (RibonanzaNet2 reportedly on ~40 million) with held-out prospective test sequences from the Kaggle challenge; state-of-the-art on reactivity and fine-tuned secondary-structure tasks.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalisation to long natural RNAs and to structural ensembles rather than single averaged reactivity profiles.

existing_models.name: DREEM, DRACO and DANCE-MaP (read-clustering methods that deconvolve probing data into several conformations and their populations)
existing_models.score_and_split: Validated on in-silico mixtures and on bacterial riboswitches and SARS-CoV-2 elements; no standard held-out benchmark split.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Resolving more than a few conformations, and low-coverage or short-read regimes.

backbone.name: RNA-FM or RibonanzaNet (RNA language models with open weights)
backbone.hardware: Embedding 8 sequences of under 500 nucleotides takes seconds on a laptop CPU - which is exactly the problem: there is almost nothing to embed.
backbone.licence: Repository is MIT; RNA-FM and RibonanzaNet weights are openly downloadable.

integration.partner_dataset: Stanford Ribonanza / RNA Mapping Database (RMDB): ~1.1 million sequences with DMS and 2A3 reactivity profiles
integration.join_key: RNA sequence string (no stable identifier is shared; matching would be by sequence)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do sequence-to-reactivity models trained on a million short designed RNAs transfer to long natural structured RNAs measured at several probe concentrations? - a real question, but it would be a project about the Ribonanza data using these 8 molecules only as a thin test set.

controls.positive_control: DMS reacts almost only with A and C nucleotides - I confirmed in the files that G/U positions carry near-zero mutation rates, so any pipeline must recover the A/C-versus-G/U contrast.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle reactivity values within each molecule and confirm structure scores collapse; the repository's own demo already holds one of three sequences out.
controls.external_validation: RMDB / Ribonanza reactivity profiles, and the NMR-derived dissociation constant for the adenine riboswitch cited in the paper.

honest_claim_h3: Any model trained on this data could only claim: across eight RNA molecules probed in two or three laboratories, these fitted physical parameters reproduce measured DMS reactivity and the single published reference structure - with no basis for claiming the parameters hold for unseen RNAs.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use RNA sequence and chemical-probing signal to predict which structures the RNA folds into and in what proportions.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-nucleotide chemical-probing mutation rates measured at six probe concentrations in two replicates, for eight RNA molecules totalling 2,259 nucleotides (counted in the files).
plain_idea.predict: The population (fraction of molecules) of each candidate secondary structure; truth comes from cryo-EM-guided or nuclear magnetic resonance structures for a handful of these RNAs, which do not themselves report populations.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Labs doing chemical probing would get structure ensembles instead of single averaged profiles; even a failure would quantify how far physics-based parameters transfer between RNAs.

more_or_better_data.why: This repository holds 8 RNA molecules and 2,259 distinct nucleotides, which I counted in the files; RibonanzaNet was trained on roughly 1.1 million sequences with the same kind of DMS reactivity measurement. The only genuinely new data is 12 nanopore runs of one 148-nucleotide designed construct.

confidence_score.why: Two replicates at each of six probe concentrations do let you estimate measurement noise per nucleotide, which reactivity predictors generally do not report - but with 8 molecules there is no way to calibrate confidence across sequence space.

models_beatable.why: MERGE-RNA (2026) is open, MIT-licensed and reproducible with scripts; RibonanzaNet2 is a 2025 open-weight model trained on millions of profiles; DREEM/DRACO/DANCE-MaP cover ensemble deconvolution. Several open, reproducible models already serve this task.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first and third conditions: our model would not see everything MERGE-RNA sees plus more (the extra data, Ribonanza, is a different assay protocol on different molecules), and there is no shared evaluation split - 8 molecules cannot support one.

ml_idea: The project considered was: learn the mapping from chemical-probing reactivity to secondary-structure ensemble populations with a neural model instead of MERGE-RNA's handful of physical parameters, trained on the probing data in this repository. It dies on sample size - 8 RNA molecules. The viable version of this question belongs to a different dataset: take the ~1.1 million Ribonanza reactivity profiles as training data and use these 8 long natural RNAs purely as an out-of-distribution test set.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from files I actually parsed: the whole dataset is 24 MB and the eight sequences are under 500 nucleotides each, so everything fits in memory; the 3 hours is the time to write a reader for the RNAFramework .rc binary format (I wrote a working one in one pass using the loader in merge_rna/experiment.py as the spec).
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct RNA molecules with both probing data and a reference structure. I did it: 8 molecules with probing, 4 with a reference secondary structure, 5 systems in the paper's training set. That count kills the project in ten minutes.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 on verified counts: the repository contains chemical-probing data for exactly 8 RNA molecules (2,259 distinct nucleotides, reference structures for only 4), and the 25,560 nucleotide-by-condition rows are those same 8 molecules remeasured at six probe concentrations in two replicates. The paper is a well-engineered, openly licensed physics model, not a dataset - its value is as a baseline or a test case, and the new experimental deposit is 12 nanopore runs of a single designed construct. The field also already has several open, reproducible models (MERGE-RNA itself, RibonanzaNet/RibonanzaNet2, DREEM/DRACO/DANCE-MaP), so there is no crowded-field edge to offset the sample size.
